works.title: StrategyR
works.subtitle: Market research platform for Global Industry Analysts
works.excerpt: Turning three decades of analyst-driven market research into a browsable, data-dense platform that works on every screen.
works.description: Global Industry Analysts, Inc. (GIA), operating under the StrategyR brand, is a leading publisher of off-the-shelf market research, recognised for accurate market forecasting across 34 years. The platform serves influencer-driven research across a wide range of topics with comprehensive analytics for all key geographies.
works.task: Design and build an interface that makes thousands of data-heavy research reports discoverable, comparable and readable — for a global audience, on any device.
works.challenge: Research reports carry an enormous amount of structured detail: forecasts, segments, geographies and competitor tables. Presenting that density without overwhelming the reader — and without breaking down on smaller screens — was the core design problem.
works.solution: I established a clear typographic hierarchy and a consistent spacing system, then built the interface as reusable React components with Bootstrap as the responsive foundation. Report layouts, tables and filters share the same building blocks, so new report types slot in without new design work.
works.outcome: A consistent, responsive research experience across desktop, tablet and mobile, with a component library the team continues to build on. TODO: add measurable outcomes here — traffic, engagement, or delivery-speed improvements.

works.title: MarketGlass Platform
works.subtitle: Interactive market intelligence for domain experts worldwide
works.excerpt: An interactive intelligence platform connecting domain experts across competing companies worldwide.
works.description: MarketGlass™ is an interactive market intelligence platform that connects domain experts across competitive companies worldwide, giving them a shared space to contribute to and draw from live market research.
works.task: Design the experience for a collaborative intelligence platform where expert contributors and research consumers share the same interface without getting in each other's way.
works.challenge: Two very different audiences — contributing domain experts and research consumers — needed to coexist in one product. The interface had to make contribution feel effortless while keeping consumption uncluttered.
works.solution: I mapped both journeys as separate user flows, wireframed the overlap, and prototyped the interactions before any visual design. The result separates contribution and consumption into distinct modes that share one visual language and one component set.
works.outcome: A single platform serving both audiences with consistent patterns and a documented flow that the development team could implement directly. TODO: add adoption or engagement figures if you have them.

works.title: eSmart Permit
works.subtitle: Work permit automation for contractors and enterprises
works.excerpt: A configurable web platform that turns paper-based permit and approval processes into trackable digital workflows.
works.description: eSmart Permit is a web-based solution for automating the issue of work permits to contractors. The same framework generalises to any internal approval process — licences, building permits, leasing, and customer service management such as telecom connections, utility connections and property registration.
works.task: Design an interface for multi-step approval workflows that stays clear no matter how many stages, roles or conditions a given process has.
works.challenge: Every client configures their approval chain differently. The UI had to handle a two-step permit and a twelve-step licensing process with the same components, and make the current state obvious to applicant, reviewer and approver alike.
works.solution: I designed a status-driven workflow interface around a consistent step indicator, role-aware action panels and a single reusable form system. Bootstrap plugins handled modals, accordions and carousels; jQuery drove the conditional interactions between steps.
works.outcome: A configurable workflow UI that adapts to different approval processes without redesign, replacing paper-based permit handling with a trackable digital process.

works.title: iSpatial Techno Solutions
works.subtitle: Corporate platform for enterprise process automation
works.excerpt: Presenting complex enterprise integration services in a way non-technical buyers can actually follow.
works.description: iSpatial Techno Solutions provides smart solutions that automate enterprise business processes into results-oriented systems, streamlining operations that involve integration and communication between multiple business and IT environments.
works.task: Communicate a technically complex service offering to a mixed audience of technical evaluators and business decision-makers.
works.challenge: Enterprise integration is abstract. Explaining it to a business audience without either oversimplifying for the technical reader or losing the non-technical one required careful structuring of the content itself, not just the layout.
works.solution: I restructured the information architecture around outcomes rather than technology, then designed a layered layout — a plain-language summary up front with technical depth available on demand for readers who want it.
works.outcome: A corporate platform that serves both audiences from the same pages, with a responsive, cross-browser-tested front end.
